main_text.p: permutans, dextram quidem in iuniori, sinistram vero in senioris caput imponens. Et Tertullianum in ista ipsa re: Impositis & intermutatis manibus De Baptism. cap. VIII. benedixit, & quidem ita transversim obliquatis inter se, ut Christum deformantes, jam tunc portenderent benedictionem in Christum futuram. Quomodo Christum deformârunt illæ manus? imò Crucem: & sic mihi libido aliquando legere: sed refræno, & accipio Christum crucifixum. Hæc illa est quâ Andræanam hodie dicimus, validâ & satis veteri famâ diuum istum in eâ cruciatum. Anne verâ? facit me ut ambigam Martyrologium Romanum: in quo hoc saltem *legas, in Cruce suspensum. & magis Hippolytus, qui scribit In Comment. Græc. in Achaiâ Crucifixum Patris in arborem olivæ rectum. Quid magis contrà famam? Atque hæc fixio ad Simplicem nostram potiùs abeat, longè à Decussatâ.
Crux Andreana. — Vti & in Abdia lib. xxx.

page.notes: Woodcut of a figure on an X-shaped (St Andrew's) cross, captioned "Crux Andreana" in the left margin. Marginal notes: "De Baptism. cap. VIII." and "In Comment. Græc." right; "Vti & in Abdia lib. xxx." left. Some letters in the body are doubtful due to faint print; the asterisk after "*legas" and the reading of "Achaiâ" are uncertain. The printed text contains the marginal-note tags in lowercase italic and is transcribed as printed.
